The reply leans toward 95 MW, saying it is "slightly better supported," but it also says the question is "unresolved" and gives a confidence of only 35. That makes it a hedge more than a firm pick. Still, it does name B as the better-supported figure, so I read it as committing to B with a caveat.

The word "unresolved" pulls the other way and could count as declining to settle the matter. The stated confidence of 35 is low, but the reply still prefers 95 MW over 240 MW. The question is whether a weak preference is enough to count as an answer. The instruction says a reply gives B "even if it adds a caveat or mentions A," and this reply fits that.

B
